strategy.summary: Two k6 scenarios slowed past the 20% threshold and stayed slow on a rerun: orders › detail (p95 23→33 ms, p99 25→36 ms), which the bisect put on 72802a9 (it adds a second sequential store round trip, productNames, after orderLines), and search › search (p95 14→60 ms), which also fails at the last good run's commit, so the cause is outside the repo's commits (the cache/environment). Each gets a scenario-keyed threshold at its baseline +20% beside the scripts' existing thresholds, plus a recorded and filed defect. Existing scripts are only extended, nothing restructured.
inScope: Scenario-keyed http_req_duration thresholds in perf/orders.js (detail p95, p99) and perf/search.js (search p95)
Recording and filing one defect per slowed scenario
outOfScope: Changing application code to win the time back (a person's work)
The list scenario, which did not slow
Restructuring the existing k6 scripts beyond adding thresholds and the ticket tag
assumptions: Thresholds are the baseline medians from the work item with 20% headroom: detail p95 23 ms → p(95)<27.6, detail p99 25 ms → p(99)<30, search p95 14 ms → p(95)<16.8.

run_tests runs the scripts in smoke mode with --no-thresholds against BASE_URL=http://localhost:4310, so the counted runs prove the scripts still run, not the thresholds; the thresholds bite under the scripts' own load.
The app runs for real (the run's environment starts it at BASE_URL); nothing is faked.
openQuestions: search's slowdown is present at the last good run's commit too; src/search.js models cache misses that rebuild the index and says 'longer still on a bad day' — whether the cache's miss rate or rebuild time changed in the environment needs a person to investigate.

risks.description: A threshold set at the slow value would hide the regression
risks.mitigation: Thresholds are set from the baseline medians plus 20%, so the scripts fail under load until the app is fast again.

risks.description: An unkeyed threshold would hold the list scenario to detail's numbers

acceptanceCriteria.text: perf/orders.js fails when the detail scenario's p95 latency exceeds 27.6 ms or its p99 exceeds 30 ms (baseline 23/25 ms +20%)
perf/search.js fails when the search scenario's p95 latency exceeds 16.8 ms (baseline 14 ms +20%)
No existing threshold, check or scenario is dropped or loosened
acceptanceCriteria.metBy: The new thresholds are added beside the existing http_req_failed and http_req_duration thresholds, which stay unchanged.

testCases.title: detail scenario holds p95 under 27.6 ms and p99 under 30 ms
steps: Run perf/orders.js under its constant-arrival-rate load
testCases.expected: http_req_duration{scenario:detail} p(95)<27.6 and p(99)<30 pass once the app is back at baseline; fail now (p95 33 ms, p99 36 ms)
testCases.rationale: Guards the regression from 72802a9 'Show each line's product name on an order': GET /orders/:id now awaits productNames() as a separate store round trip (~6-9 ms) after orderLines(), instead of fetching the names in the same query as the lines as the commit message claims — 3 sequential round trips instead of 2.

testCases.title: search scenario holds p95 under 16.8 ms
steps: Run perf/search.js under its constant-arrival-rate load
testCases.expected: http_req_duration{scenario:search} p(95)<16.8 passes once search is back at baseline; fails now (p95 60 ms)
testCases.rationale: Guards search p95 14→60 ms. Not bisectable: it fails at the last good commit 74ba3b2 too, so the change is in the environment/data; src/search.js's cache misses rebuild the index (40 ms + exponential tail), so a higher miss rate or slower rebuild would push p95 to that range.

defects.title: Order detail slowed: p95 23→33 ms, p99 25→36 ms after 72802a9 adds a second store round trip
defects.description: perf/orders.js › detail (GET /orders/:id): p95 latency 23 ms → 33 ms (+45%, 34 ms on rerun), p99 25 ms → 36 ms (+47.6%, 35 ms on rerun), against the median of the last 5 good runs. The bisect found 72802a9 "Show each line's product name on an order" as the first slow commit. In src/app.js the route now awaits productNames(...) after orderLines(...), and src/store.js productNames does its own roundTrip() (6–9 ms). The detail request goes from 2 sequential store queries (findOrder, orderLines) to 3, about +50%, which matches the slowdown. The commit message says the names come "in one query with the lines", but they come in a separate query. Fix: return the product name from orderLines (it already looks up each line's product for priceCents), or otherwise join the names into the lines' query. The new threshold http_req_duration{scenario:detail} p(95)<27.6, p(99)<30 fails until then.
defects.evidence: TestForge baseline vs current under the script's own load (20 req/s, 10 s): p95 23→33 ms (rerun 34), p99 25→36 ms (rerun 35). The bisect's first slow commit is 72802a9fba0d.

defects.title: Search slowed: p95 14→60 ms, already at the last good run's commit (environment/data change)
defects.description: perf/search.js › search (GET /search?q=): p95 latency 14 ms → 60 ms (+333%, 55 ms on rerun), against the median of the last 5 good runs. The bisect couldn't find a commit, because the slowdown also shows at the last good run's commit 74ba3b2. The cause is outside the repo's commits: the app's environment, its data, or the shared search cache. In src/search.js a cache hit costs one store round trip (6–9 ms). A miss sleeps rebuildMs() (40 ms plus an exponential tail with a 25 ms mean) before it queries the store. A p95 of ~60 ms means more than 5% of searches now miss, or rebuilds have got slower. A person should check the shared cache's hit rate and expiry, and the index rebuild time, in the environment. The threshold http_req_duration{scenario:search} p(95)<16.8 fails until search is fast again.
defects.evidence: TestForge baseline vs current under the script's own load (20 req/s, 10 s): p95 14→60 ms, 55 ms on the rerun. It also fails at 74ba3b2881e6, the last good run's commit, so it couldn't be bisected.
